balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Swire Properties Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Swire Properties Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: Reported EPS, underlying EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
Reported EPS is statutory net income per share. Underlying EPS is underlying profit (ex investment-property revaluation and disposal gains) per share -- the measure management uses to set the dividend. DPS is the cash dividend paid per share.

For Swire Properties Limited: reported EPS was negative in FY2024 (-HK$0.13) and FY2025 (-HK$0.27) while underlying EPS was positive and growing (HK$1.49 in FY2025); the dividend tracks underlying EPS (target ~50% payout of underlying profit), not reported EPS.

What to watch:

  • Dividend versus underlying EPS payout ratio, not reported EPS
  • Whether the dividend (already exceeding recurring underlying EPS in some years) is sustained by divestment gains

fcf.title: Net income, underlying profit and owner FCF
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Underlying profit is the company's own non-GAAP measure, excluding non-cash investment-property revaluation and disposal gains. Owner FCF (the DCF's base) is Recurring Underlying Profit -- underlying profit further stripped of one-off divestment gains -- which is already post-interest and post-tax.

For Swire Properties Limited: net income swung to losses in FY2024 (-HK$766m) and FY2025 (-HK$1,533m) purely on investment-property fair-value declines, while underlying profit kept growing (+27% YoY in FY2025). The valuation is built on the underlying-profit line, not reported net income.

What to watch:

  • Underlying profit trend, not the reported net income swings
  • Recurring underlying profit (ex one-off disposal gains) versus the headline underlying profit figure

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Swire Properties Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Swire Properties Limited: CapEx here is overwhelmingly additions to investment property under construction (the HK$100bn Hong Kong/Mainland development plan), not plant & equipment -- PPE additions alone (CapexPPE in the CSV) are a small fraction of the total, so this chart is dominated by the development pipeline, not maintenance spend.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Swire Properties Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

underlyingProfit.title: Underlying profit vs reported profit
underlyingProfit.content:
Swire Properties revalues its investment property through profit or loss every period under HKFRS. Underlying profit is the company's audited non-GAAP measure that excludes those non-cash fair-value movements and gains/losses on investment-property disposals; recurring underlying profit additionally excludes one-off divestment gains (e.g. Brickell City Centre, Tsing Yi, One Island East). Reported net income includes all of it.

For Swire Properties Limited: reported net income was negative for two consecutive years (FY2024: -HK$766m; FY2025: -HK$1,533m) purely on investment-property fair-value losses, even as underlying profit rose (+27% YoY to HK$8,620m in FY2025, largely one-off disposal gains) and recurring underlying profit fell slightly (-3% to HK$6,260m) on rising net finance costs. The DCF capitalises recurring underlying profit, not reported net income.

What to watch:

  • Recurring underlying profit trend (the cleanest read on the core landlord business) versus the headline underlying profit figure, which can be flattered by one-off disposal gains
  • Whether reported net income losses reflect genuine cap-rate/rental deterioration or just mark-to-market noise

ipRevaluation.title: Investment property fair-value change
ipRevaluation.content:
The change in fair value of investment property recognised through profit or loss each period, before tax and non-controlling interests. This single line is the primary driver of the gap between reported net income and underlying profit.

For Swire Properties Limited: attributable fair-value losses were HK$5,996m (FY2024) and HK$6,095m (FY2025), driven by Hong Kong and Mainland office cap-rate expansion and soft rental assumptions; H1 FY2026 recorded a small gain (HK$578m) as markets stabilised. Management explicitly states these non-cash movements have no impact on operating cash flow, underlying profit, or investment strategy.

What to watch:

  • Direction (gain vs loss) as a read on cap-rate sentiment, not cash generation
  • Magnitude relative to book equity -- cumulative attributable fair-value losses were ~HK$28.6bn FY2020-25

bookValue.title: Book value per share
bookValue.content:
Shareholders' equity attributable to the company, divided by shares outstanding. For a fair-value landlord this is close to appraisal NAV: Hong Kong investment property is carried at 2.6-5.5% cap rates and Mainland property at 5.5-6.5%.

For Swire Properties Limited: book value per share has declined from HK$49.85 (FY2021) to HK$46.80 (FY2025) as cumulative investment-property fair-value losses and dividends exceeding underlying profit have outpaced retained earnings growth. The stock trades around 0.4-0.5x this book value -- the DCF's cost-of-equity capitalisation of recurring underlying profit lands well below book NAV because no equity investor can earn the low cap rates baked into the appraisal values; the gap is the value of capital recycling (selling assets near appraisal) that the earnings-based model does not credit.

What to watch:

  • Whether book value stabilises as the HK$100bn investment plan matures and fair-value losses slow
  • The price/book discount versus history (10-year range ~0.30x-0.64x; current ~0.41x)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Swire Properties Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Swire Properties Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
